subject: Vendor license update: Verida Insights - data license & SLA changes
messages:
From: Sue Hart <sue.hart@veridatainsights.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@veridatainsights.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming license changes & draft SOW (Verida Insights)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the partnership this past year. I wanted to flag a few upcoming changes on our side that affect licensing and delivery SLA for the product enrichment feed you consume:

- Pricing: standard per-record unit will shift +8% as of July 1 unless a 12-month commitment is signed by June 15.
- Delivery SLA: we will be introducing a 24-hour freshness SLA for delta updates (current best effort).
- License language: we updated our standard data license to add a clause about derivative models and downstream redistribution; customers can request carve-outs.

I've attached a draft SOW (Verida_SOW_v3.pdf) and an updated pricing matrix. Can we schedule a short call next week to walk through the changes and any carve-outs Redwood needs for internal tooling/evals?

If you prefer to handle edits directly, I can generate a DocuSign packet once we agree on the scope/term.

Best,
Sue
Sue Hart
Head of Customer Success | Verida Insights
[sample-data-delivery.txt attached]

---

Note: this is an initial notice; procurement@veridatainsights.com is copied for contracting follow-up.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Upcoming license changes & draft SOW (Verida Insights)

Folks — forwarding Sue's note. TL;DR: vendor is pushing price +8% and a new clause on derivative models. I think we should push back on the redistribution/derivatives language and try for a 9–12 month fixed price to avoid the July increase.

Key asks for today:
- Marcus: can legal review the license carve-out on derivative models? This impacts model evals where we use the enrichment to train internal rerankers.
- Lauren: procurement — can you ask for a 60-day grace on pricing or an early-commit discount?
- Karthik: engineering — how much do we rely on sub-day deltas vs daily? If we can tolerate 24-hour SLA that simplifies negotiations.

I've attached the draft SOW and the sample delivery file for quick validation. Planning a short sync Thu 5/14 11am PT — lmk if that works.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — 11am PT works for me. A couple notes after a quick look at the SOW/pricing matrix:

- Procurement stance: we can consider a 12-month commitment but need a cap on annual price increases and a right to terminate if data quality drops below defined SLAs.
- For the derivative models clause, we generally accept training for internal model improvements but not rights for the vendor to claim ownership or additional fees for models we build. Legal should propose specific carve-out language.
- On the price increase: ask for a grandfathered rate through the end of the 12-month term if we commit now; if not, negotiate a phased ramp (4% first 6 months, then +4% thereafter).

I'll add a procurement redline and share before the call.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Lead, Strategic Procurement | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Upcoming license changes & draft SOW (Verida Insights)

Naomi — thanks for the quick coordination and for looping your team. A few counterpoints from our side:

- Pricing flexibility: we're willing to offer a 10% discount on the new rate if Redwood signs a 12-month committed SOW by June 15; otherwise the +8% baseline stands.
- Derivatives carve-out: we can accept a carve-out for internal model training limited to non-commercial redistribution, but we'd like the right to reference improvements in our marketing (anonymized).
- SLA: the 24-hour freshness SLA will only apply to customers on committed terms; otherwise we'll keep best-effort.

I've attached a marked-up SOW (Verida_SOW_v3.pdf) with suggested language for the carve-out. If legal can propose redline text, we can exchange versions faster.

Happy to keep the Thursday call — if it makes sense we can convert to a contracting call and include procurement.

Best,
Sue

Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming license changes & draft SOW (Verida Insights) — proposed final points

Sue / Verida procurement team — thanks for the markup and the discount proposal. After internal discussions we can provisionally agree to a 12-month committed SOW with the following final points before we ask legal to sign off:

1) Pricing: accept the vendor's new baseline with the offered 10% discount if signed by June 15; confirm the pricing table in pricing_matrix_Q3.xlsx (attached).
2) Derivatives clause: legal to insert carve-out language that permits internal model training and evals for product improvements, prohibits vendor claims to our derived models, and excludes commercial redistribution. We won't agree to vendor marketing rights to reference model improvements tied specifically to Redwood usage.
3) SLA: accept 24-hour freshness SLA tied to committed accounts; include a service credit schedule for >24h breaches (1% monthly credit per 12h breach, capped at 30%).
4) Sample validation: we'll run a 48-hour sample validation window (sample-data-delivery.txt attached). Any systematic quality regressions will allow us to pause ingest and pursue remediation credits.

Next steps: Lauren, please circulate the procurement redline. Marcus/Karthik, can legal/engineering provide final redline language by EOD Mon 5/31 so we can get this to DocuSign and hit the June 15 commitment window?

If Verida can prep the DocuSign packet with the attached SOW/Pricing and mark the expiration date, we'll route for signature as soon as internal redlines are applied.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
